extDescription.message: What happens after you reject cookies: compares your choice with the cookies and trackers it observes. Nothing leaves your browser.

openSite.message: Open a website (http or https) and try again.

noRequestData.message: No data about this page's requests.

footerNote.message: Tracker cookies are the ones the browser sends when the page contacts them. They may have been stored while visiting other sites: that is how a tracker can recognise the same person across sites.

groupNote_Identifier.message: Unknown to the database, but stored on another site's domain, sent to any site that contacts it (SameSite=None) and valid for at least $DAYS$ days: the typical shape of an identifier that follows a person across sites. It is a hint, not a classification.

compareSites.message: Third-party sites that can recognise you

compareNote.message: “At your choice” counts everything already there when you chose, so before your consent or refusal. “Now” only counts trackers contacted afterwards: reload the page for a complete measure.

verdictHeading_rejected.message: You rejected at $TIME$. What happened next:

verdictHeading_accepted.message: You accepted at $TIME$. This is what is active:

verdictHeading_partial.message: You made a partial choice at $TIME$. This is what is active:

verdictHeadingNone.message: No choice recorded in this session. If you have not chosen yet, this is what is already active:

itemTcfRecorded.message: The site's consent signal (TCF), read by its advertising partners, records your rejection: $CONSENTED$ of $TOTAL$ purposes with consent.

itemTcfRecordedNoTotal.message: The site's consent signal (TCF), read by its advertising partners, records your rejection: no purpose with consent.

itemClickOnly.message: You clicked “$LABEL$”. We cannot check how the site recorded the choice.

itemLegitimate_one.message: According to the same signal, $COUNT$ purpose remains active on “legitimate interest”, which does not ask for consent.

itemLegitimate_other.message: According to the same signal, $COUNT$ purposes remain active on “legitimate interest”, which does not ask for consent.

itemNoThirdParty.message: We see no cookies a third-party site could use to recognise you here.

itemThirdPartyStill_other.message: $COUNT$ third-party sites can still recognise you on this site:

itemThirdPartyNoChoice_other.message: With no consent recorded, $COUNT$ third-party sites can already recognise you:

itemThirdParty_other.message: $COUNT$ third-party sites can recognise you on this site:

itemSiteMarketing_other.message: $COUNT$ of the site's cookies are classified as marketing:

verdictRespected.message: Your rejection seems to be respected.

verdictPartly.message: Your rejection seems to be only partly respected.

verdictNeedReload.message: Reload the page for a complete check.

verdictAccepted.message: You accepted: the above is active after your consent.

verdictPartialChoice.message: With a partial choice we cannot tell which of these cookies fall within what you accepted.

disclaimer.message: Automatic indication based on what your browser observes. It may be incomplete or wrong and is not a legal assessment.

compareDetails.message: Details: at your choice and now

noteOwnPlatform.message: Classified as marketing because of its use on other sites; here, on the site that creates it, we cannot tell what it is for.

noteShortLived.message: Short-lived: on its own it cannot recognise you on later days.

groupExplain_Marketing.message: According to the database, used for advertising: to show you ads and measure their effect, often by following you across sites.

groupExplain_Analytics.message: According to the database, used to count visits and understand how the site is used.

groupExplain_Unknown.message: Our database does not know them: we cannot tell what they are for.

groupExplain_Personalization.message: According to the database, used to tailor content to you, for example recommendations.

groupExplain_Preferences.message: According to the database, they remember your settings, such as language or currency.

groupExplain_Functional.message: According to the database, they make parts of the site work, such as the cart or remembering your cookie choice.

groupExplain_Necessary.message: According to the database, essential for the site to work, for example to keep you logged in.

groupExplain_Security.message: According to the database, they protect the site and your account, for example against fraudulent logins.

itemThirdPartyPartitioned_other.message: $COUNT$ third-party sites have cookies kept for this site only: they can recognise you when you come back here, not on other sites:

notePartitioned.message: Kept for this site only (partitioned): it does not follow you to other sites.

itemSignedIn.message: You are signed in to these services: they receive your account cookies when the page loads their content, whatever you choose in the banner:
